subject: Dedicated capacity commit: term options, ramp schedule, and start gates (Aster Technologies)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Rao <maya.rao@astertech.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: term options, ramp schedule, and target start dates

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the time yesterday. As discussed, I'm putting a concise set of options on the table so your finance and procurement teams can compare tradeoffs quickly. High level: Aster asked for predictable throughput for inference workloads (low-90s percentile latency targets for 16k context), a 99.9% regional uptime SLA, and a committed pool for steady-state traffic.

Option A — 12-month commit (fast start)
- Committed capacity: 12 A100-equivalent GPU pool (shared across models)
- Throughput guarantee: baseline of 110 requests/sec for your standard ensemble (our perf team will validate with the workload snapshot)
- Discount: 10% off list hosted Dedicated rates
- Ramp schedule: 50% of committed capacity active by week 1, 100% by week 6
- Start date: target Sept 1, 2026

Option B — 24-month commit (balanced)
- Committed capacity: 14 A100-equivalent GPUs
- Throughput guarantee: 130 requests/sec baseline
- Discount: 18% off list rates
- Ramp schedule: 30% active month 1, 70% month 2, 100% by month 4
- Start date: Sept 15 or Oct 1 (flexible)

Option C — 36-month commit (best unit economics)
- Committed capacity: 16 A100-equivalent GPUs
- Throughput guarantee: 150 requests/sec baseline + priority bursting policy
- Discount: 26% off list rates
- Ramp schedule: soft-start (20% month 1) with guaranteed full activation by month 4
- Start date: Oct 1 preferred; possible earlier start with a one-time implementation credit

Notes and levers we can use:
- Early-start credit: if you sign and start by Sept 1 we can waive the first invoice month for Options A/B (or apply equivalent credit for C).
- GPU sizing: Grace attached a preliminary sizing workbook — we can shift one A100-equivalent between commit buckets if the perf tests show lower peak concurrency.
- Fallback policy: automatic routing to compatible variant (lower-cost quantized model) if latency would otherwise breach the SLO during transient spikes.
- DocuSign: we'll provide an SOW + order form once you pick a term; typical turnaround is 2–4 business days for our standard paperwork.

Next step: can you share your preferred term and whether procurement prefers an earlier start for credit incentives? If helpful, Neha can run a quick redline preview with legal on any standard clauses.

Best,
Rishi
Head of Sales, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
attachments: gpu-sizing-estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Maya Rao <maya.rao@astertech.com>

Cc: procure@astertech.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: term options, ramp schedule, and target start dates

Thanks Rishi — this is really helpful. A couple of clarifying q's from procurement and infra: 

1) For the throughput guarantee numbers, are those steady-state guarantees or do they include burst windows? We need a clear definition for SLA measurement and a sample reporting cadence.
2) Is the early-start credit conditional on a signed order, or on physical capacity activation? Procurement prefers credit on signed contract date.
3) For Option C, can you confirm whether the priority bursting policy includes cross-region fallbacks? We want to avoid region failover without explicit consent.

On budget: the CFO team prefers the 24-month face because it balances cost and optionality, but they're asking for an example invoice schedule and a clearer breakdown of what the discount applies to (compute hours vs management/observability add-ons).

If possible please send an estimated invoice ladder + a short sample SLA paragraph we can share with legal.

Regards,
Maya Rao
VP Platform Engineering
Aster Technologies
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Rao <maya.rao@astertech.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: term options, ramp schedule, and target start dates

Hi Maya — looping in a couple notes to directly address your questions so procurement has language for review.

1) SLA / throughput measurement: our guarantee is measured as percentile throughput over rolling 24-hour windows for the committed pool. Bursts beyond baseline are allowed and are subject to a priority-burst policy; we can define a burst credit or hard-throttle during extreme events depending on the term. We'll provide a sample SLA paragraph — see the draft below.

Draft SLA excerpt (for procurement):
"Redwood will provision a Dedicated GPU pool as specified in the Order Form. Redwood guarantees a baseline throughput (requests/sec) as measured at the pool ingress at the 95th percentile over a rolling 24-hour period. In events where sustained traffic exceeds the baseline and impacts measured latency, Redwood will invoke the configured burst policy; Redwood will provide daily and monthly usage and performance reports and notify the customer within one business hour for any sustained degradation. Remedies for SLA breach are service credits as defined in Section 5 of the Order Form."

2) Early-start credit: we are happy to accept procurement's preference — the credit can be applied on the signed contract date rather than physical activation (we'll reflect that in the order form).

3) Cross-region fallback: for Option C the priority bursting policy can include cross-region routing, but only with explicit customer opt-in. Default is single-region with intra-region fallbacks.

Attached: short invoice ladder template and a one-page invoice example showing compute, reserved commit credit, and optional Redwood Console observability fee.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call to review the invoice ladder with the CFO; Rishi / Jordan — would you be available tomorrow morning?

Cheers,
Neha
Senior Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference
attachments: sample_invoice_ladder.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: term options, ramp schedule, and target start dates

Maya — thanks for the quick review and great questions. Aster's CFO preference for 24 months makes sense. Below is a concrete counterproposal that tries to balance their asks with improved unit economics: 

Counterproposal (24-month primary, 12-month fallback):
- Term: 24 months primary (deal id AST-4721-RW)
- Committed pool: 14 A100-equivalent GPUs (as in Option B)
- Effective discount: 20% on compute component (we can increase from 18% if we lock the Sept 15 start date and sign within 5 business days)
- Observability/console: waived for first 3 months; then standard fee applies (line-item on invoices)
- Ramp: 30% month 1, 70% month 2, 100% month 4; we will provide a staging pool to test performance during month 0 (pre-start)
- Start-credit: signed contract date triggers one-month credit on the first invoice if signed by Aug 31; otherwise credit applies on activation
- SLA language: use the draft Neha included (we'll add exact credit schedule in Section 5)

Operational asks from our side:
- Access to a 48-hour workload snapshot for perf validation (Grace will coordinate)
- Account mapping for roles so we can set RBAC and telemetry dashboards ahead of activation

If procurement confirms acceptance, we'll convert the SOW to an order form and send via DocuSign. Jordan — I'll need your help to finalize the pricing table and payment milestone schedule.

Thanks,
Rishi

- Confirm the maximum allowed burst (in RPS) before the priority-burst policy will kick in; procurement wants a hard threshold documented.
- Grace — we'll send the 48-hour workload snapshot to your secure upload link by EOD Friday.

If those are in the order form, we can route to legal and likely sign within 3 business days.

Thanks,
Maya
